scope: Five measured experiments; preflight observations listed separately. No benchmark or Cargo process was run during independent recalculation.

method.quantile: Nearest rank: sorted sample at 1-based ceil(n*p/100), independently using integer arithmetic.
method.mean: Exact integer sum divided by sample count using Decimal, compared exactly to each CSV field.
method.reported_comparisons: Median across process-round statistics for each variant; change=(candidate/baseline-1)*100. Four rounds except two-round unchanged control. Means below are medians of per-round means.
method.no_discard_check: Every case in every recorded measurement process retains exactly observation IDs 0..999, in order; all raw groups match the complete summary and execution logs. No failing, missing or extra process is present in the recorded five experiments.
method.allocation_semantics: Separate operation invocation; successful alloc + alloc_zeroed + realloc calls and full requested realloc capacity; includes result destruction. Requested bytes are allocation traffic, not live/peak memory.
method.comparison_tuple: [baseline value, candidate value, percentage change]; time values are nanoseconds. Percentages rounded to 8 decimals for this compact artifact; all CSV checks were exact.
method.allocation_statistics: Allocation fields show per-round P50 medians; constant_in_all_samples=true also verifies p50/p95/p99/mean and every raw observation are identical for each variant.

source_provenance.legacy_metadata_baseline_revision: 070e9cf727a31a8ee23ffd372d7dc9e378cbfdfc is the harness historical reference, not the revision of either measured binary. The metadata variant=candidate is the baked harness feature, not the experimental baseline/candidate role.

input_fingerprints.other_items: The four derived byte sequences inner_mso, canonical_mso, issuer_sig_structure and device_authentication have identical recorded size/hash pairs across all 36 measurement and 2 preflight processes; their bytes were not independently reconstructed during this review.

report_review.display_tolerance: 0.0005 microseconds for 3-decimal times; 0.005 percentage points for 2-decimal percentages; allocation calls and bytes exact.
report_review.interpretation: The report correctly keeps the owned MSO regression, canonical/transcript regressions, response allocation traffic increase and full-issuance regression visible, and avoids treating the small full-verification P50 difference as a speedup. Tail/control values are supplied here for the final report.

key_findings: All 4,032 summary statistics match raw samples exactly; no recorded observation is missing, duplicated or excluded. All 36 measured processes and 2 preflights returned zero.

Current borrowed versus owned response parsing: CPU P50 -19.9363%, allocation calls 100 to 41, requested bytes 13,570 to 5,396. MSO parsing: CPU P50 -18.8722%, allocation calls 43 to 16, requested bytes 4,577 to 2,520.

Current borrowed versus owned full verification: CPU P50 -0.4182%, allocation calls 83 to 51 and requested bytes 11,734 to 6,714. The timing difference does not establish an overall speedup on this shared host.

Current owned MSO parsing versus previous main regresses CPU P50 by 17.2144% (5,934 to 6,955.5 ns), with paired-round regressions of 15.8526% to 18.6959%; allocation calls still fall 64 to 43. This regression must remain visible.

Other previous-main comparisons include canonical encoding CPU P50 +7.5806%, transcript validation +4.8662%, owned response allocation traffic +5.1123%, and complete issuance CPU P50 +1.5356%. Lower allocations do not establish lower CPU time.

Same previous binary control ranges across cases: CPU P50 -11.7485% to +3.2106%; CPU P99 -70.9950% to +29.9356%. Full-verification control P50 +3.2106% and P99 +14.5323%. These are observed variation ranges, not confidence intervals or corrections.

Current owned versus previous-main full verification CPU P50 -2.0775% but P99 +6.8929%; complete issuance P99 +30.5097%; external signing control P99 +29.7052%; IssuerSigned encoding P99 +32.1202%. All tails remain included; neither speedups nor regressions in noisy tails should be attributed to one code change.

The five experiments use identical seven-item recorded input fingerprints. Actual binaries, retained response bytes, transcript bytes and Annex source bytes are independently rehashed. Current and old source manifests match their build commits; the old library source/manifest subset matches previous main byte for byte.
